text: 57-year-old male presents with 3-month history of progressive epigastric pain radiating to back, early satiety, and 25-lb unintentional weight loss. Patient reports new-onset diabetes mellitus diagnosed 2 months ago. Denies jaundice but notes dark urine and pale stools over past 2 weeks. Family history notable for pancreatic cancer in mother at age 62 and ovarian cancer in sister at age 48 (BRCA positive family). Social history: Never smoker, occasional alcohol use. Physical exam: thin, cachectic appearance, jaundice noted, palpable epigastric mass. Labs show elevated total bilirubin 4.2 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 3.5 mg/dL, elevated alkaline phosphatase 420 U/L, CA 19-9 markedly elevated at 1250 U/mL. Urgent CT abdomen ordered. High suspicion for pancreatic malignancy.
